🐈‍⬛VRAMSweep.description: Release GPU VRAM on demand and return a STRING report of what was recovered. Two toggles choose the release scope (unload models, sweep CUDA caches); Force GC adds an extra collect + synchronize. Each stage is isolated, so one failing does not abort the rest.

offload_model.name: Unload models
offload_model.tooltip: Unload all models from VRAM before releasing.

force_gc.name: Force GC
force_gc.tooltip: Run an extra gc.collect() + cuda.synchronize() afterwards for a deeper squeeze.

anything.name: anything
anything.tooltip: Optional value passed through unchanged, so this node can sit inside a chain.

1.name: report
1.tooltip: Text report of how much VRAM was released.

🐈‍⬛RAMReclaim.description: Reclaim physical memory on demand and return a STRING report of what was recovered. Three toggles pick the passes (file cache, process working sets, own DLLs); Retry times repeats them. Dry Run reports the baseline without trimming. Windows-only (ctypes); no-ops elsewhere.

clean_file_cache.name: Clean file cache
clean_file_cache.tooltip: Trim the system file cache. Needs administrator rights; silently skipped when it fails.

clean_dlls.name: Trim own DLLs
clean_dlls.tooltip: Trim this process's own loaded DLLs.

retry_times.name: Retry times
retry_times.tooltip: How many times to repeat the selected pass(es).

dry_run.name: Dry Run
dry_run.tooltip: Skip the actual trimming and only report the current physical-memory baseline.

anything.name: anything
anything.tooltip: Optional value passed through unchanged, so this node can sit inside a chain.

1.name: report
1.tooltip: Text report of how much RAM was reclaimed.

🐈‍⬛H3ImageToVideo.description: Image-/text-to-video conditioning for MiniMax H3 with dual-stage outputs. Stage-1 uses 'positive' + 'av_latent' built at width/height; Stage-2 (refine) uses 'positive2', a separate conditioning object baked at stage2_width/stage2_height so its keyframes line up with the upscaled latent. For t2v (no keyframes) positive2 is an independent copy and the stage2 resolution is unused. Do NOT fan a single output to two samplers — the H3 sampler mutates keyframes in place.

stage2_height.name: stage2_height
stage2_height.tooltip: Stage-2 (refine) target height. Ignored for t2v (no keyframes).

🐈‍⬛AnySwitch.description: Generic single-active-input switch for ANY data type. Wire several branch outputs in at once; at runtime forward the single one that carries data and raise an error if none or more than one is populated. The first connection decides the node's type: the front end then locks every port to that same type and labels every port as <type>_<index> and the output with the type name, so the node visibly shows what it switches. Ports grow automatically as you connect (two by default, one extra empty slot each time, up to nine). Flip the active branch upstream — no rewiring, no toggle.

🐈‍⬛GroupControl.description: Open or close canvas groups from a single panel. Each group on the canvas (including subgraphs) becomes a row with its name and one toggle; the list can be filtered by group colour and name keyword and ordered by name or canvas position. A mode decides how toggles interact: free control, always exactly one open, or at most one open. Closing a group either bypasses or mutes every node inside it, which is chosen in the panel settings. The signal input is a pass-through so the node can live inside an execution chain without changing the data that flows through it; all group switching happens in the front end.

signal.name: signal
signal.tooltip: Optional pass-through. Whatever is wired here is returned unchanged so the node can sit inside a chain; it is not involved in group switching.

🐈‍⬛NodeControl.description: Open or close individual canvas nodes from a single panel. Each node on the canvas becomes a row with its title and one toggle; the list can be filtered by node colour (an uncoloured node inherits its group's colour) and by name / type keyword, and ordered by name or canvas position. A mode decides how toggles interact: free control, always exactly one open, or at most one open. Closing a node either bypasses or mutes it, which is chosen in the panel settings. Notes, reroutes, primitives and the control node itself are never listed. The signal input is a pass-through so the node can live inside an execution chain without changing the data that flows through it; all switching happens in the front end.

signal.name: signal
signal.tooltip: Optional pass-through. Whatever is wired here is returned unchanged so the node can sit inside a chain; it is not involved in node switching.

🐈‍⬛TextGenerate.description: The official Generate Text node with a multi-image socket: same text encoder, prompt, video, audio, max length, sampling panel and output, but the image slot accepts several images and the encoder reads all of them in one pass. Frames are scaled to fit a shared canvas and padded, never stretched or enlarged.

clip.tooltip: The text encoder / multimodal model that reads the prompt and the media.

prompt.name: prompt
prompt.tooltip: What to ask about the connected media.

images.name: images
images.tooltip: The image input of the official node, repeatable: connect as many images as you need and the encoder reads them in the same generation. Order follows the socket number. A video takes precedence over images, exactly as on the official node.

video.name: video
video.tooltip: Video frames as image batch. Assumed to be 24 FPS; subsampled to 1 FPS internally.

audio.name: audio
audio.tooltip: Audio for the encoder to listen to.

sampling_mode.name: Sampling Mode
sampling_mode.tooltip: Sampling on: sample with the settings below. Sampling off: greedy, always the same answer.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.tooltip: Sampling temperature. Higher is more random, lower is more deterministic. 0.7 is a balanced default.

top_k.name: Top-K
top_k.tooltip: Limit sampling to the K most likely next tokens. 0 disables the cap.

top_p.name: Top-P
top_p.tooltip: Nucleus sampling: only consider tokens whose cumulative probability reaches this cutoff.

min_p.name: Min-P
min_p.tooltip: Minimum probability floor (relative to the most likely token) a token must exceed to be sampled.

repetition_penalty.name: Repetition Penalty
repetition_penalty.tooltip: Penalizes repeated tokens to discourage loops. 1.0 = no penalty.

seed.name: Seed
seed.tooltip: Random seed for reproducible sampling. 0 = random each run.

presence_penalty.name: Presence Penalty
presence_penalty.tooltip: Penalizes tokens by whether they have appeared at all, encouraging new topics.

thinking.name: thinking

use_default_template.name: use_default_template
use_default_template.tooltip: Use the built in system prompt/template if the model has one.

mtp.name: mtp
mtp.tooltip: Speculative decoding with the checkpoint's multi-token-prediction head. No effect without MTP weights. auto adapts the draft depth; 2-5 pins it. Sampled output stays correctly distributed but differs from non-MTP output for the same seed.

🐈‍⬛ResolutionSelector.description: Calculate width and height from aspect ratio and megapixel target, with the megapixel target adjustable in steps of 0.01 (two decimal places) instead of the official node's 0.1. Useful for setting up Empty Latent Image dimensions. Pick the 'Custom' aspect ratio to enter an explicit width and height instead of a megapixel target; the megapixel input is hidden while Custom is selected. Otherwise identical to the official Resolution Selector: same aspect ratios, live resolution preview, and nearest-multiple rounding of the result.

aspect_ratio.name: Aspect Ratio
aspect_ratio.tooltip: The aspect ratio for the output dimensions. Choose 'Custom' to set an explicit width and height.

megapixels.name: Megapixels
megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels, adjustable to two decimal places (0.01 steps). 1.0 MP ≈ 1024x1024 for square. Ignored — and hidden — when the aspect ratio is 'Custom'.

preview.name: Preview

multiple.name: Multiple

custom_height.name: Height
